title: Risk stratification and multi-omics reveal RAD51 inhibition as a radiosensitizing strategy in triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: An, Ran; Li, Jianming; Liu, Tianhui; Tang, Cunyu; Lu, Hong
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦三阴性乳腺癌放疗敏感性与免疫微环境，未涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is a highly aggressive subtype characterized by significant inter- and intra-tumoral heterogeneity. Its varied response to radiotherapy limits clinical outcomes, yet the underlying molecular determinants remain poorly understood. METHODS: By integrating single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data, we profiled cell-type-specific radiosensitivity and defined distinct molecular subtypes via consensus clustering. A random survival forest (RSF) prognostic model was then constructed using 34 survival-associated genes and interpreted via SHAP analysis, and its performance was validated in multiple independent external cohorts. RAD51 was prioritized via Dependency Map (DepMap) analysis, and its functional role was validated in vitro and in vivo, supporting its role as a biological dependency in radiotherapy response. Moreover, tumor immune remodeling was further evaluated by immunofluorescence and protein analysis. RESULTS: Single-cell analysis revealed that fibroblasts, macrophages, and proliferative cells harbored elevated radioresistance signatures compared to lymphoid lineages. Bulk profiling identified two distinct subtypes: Cluster A (immunosuppressive, radioresistant, poor prognosis) and Cluster B (immune-active, favorable survival). The RSF model robustly stratified patient risk, with high-risk tumors tightly linked to an immune-desert microenvironment. DepMap analysis nominated RAD51 as a core biological dependency. Importantly, RAD51 knockdown sensitized TNBC cells to irradiation by exacerbating DNA damage, triggering G2/M phase arrest, and driving apoptosis. Consistently, in vivo RAD51 silencing synergized with radiotherapy to significantly suppress tumor growth. Notably, this combination reshaped the immunosuppressive TME, driving robust CD8(+) T cell infiltration, M1 macrophage repolarization, and adaptive PD-L1 upregulation. CONCLUSION: This integrative multi-omics study delineates the cellular and molecular landscape of TNBC radioresistance. The RSF model provides a robust tool for risk stratification, while identifying RAD51 as a potential therapeutic target to restore radiosensitivity and reverse immunosuppression, particularly in high-risk, immune-cold tumors.
abstract_zh: 背景：三阴性乳腺癌（TNBC）是一种高度侵袭性亚型，以显著的肿瘤间和肿瘤内异质性为特征。其对放疗的多样化反应限制了临床结局，但潜在的分子决定因素仍知之甚少。方法：通过整合单细胞和批量转录组数据，我们描绘了细胞类型特异性放射敏感性，并通过共识聚类定义了不同的分子亚型。随后，利用34个生存相关基因构建了随机生存森林（RSF）预后模型，并通过SHAP分析进行解释，其性能在多个独立外部队列中得到验证。通过依赖性图谱（DepMap）分析优先筛选出RAD51，并在体外和体内验证了其功能作用，支持其作为放疗反应中生物学依赖性的角色。此外，通过免疫荧光和蛋白质分析进一步评估了肿瘤免疫重塑。结果：单细胞分析显示，成纤维细胞、巨噬细胞和增殖细胞相较于淋巴谱系具有更高的放射抵抗特征。批量分析识别出两种不同亚型：集群A（免疫抑制、放射抵抗、预后不良）和集群B（免疫活跃、生存期有利）。RSF模型稳健地对患者风险进行分层，高风险肿瘤与免疫荒漠微环境紧密相关。DepMap分析提名RAD51为核心生物学依赖性。重要的是，RAD51敲低通过加剧DNA损伤、触发G2/M期阻滞并驱动凋亡，使TNBC细胞对放射增敏。一致地，体内RAD51沉默与放疗协同显著抑制肿瘤生长。值得注意的是，这种组合重塑了免疫抑制性肿瘤微环境（TME），驱动了显著的CD8(+) T细胞浸润、M1巨噬细胞重极化以及适应性PD-L1上调。结论：这项整合性多组学研究描绘了TNBC放射抵抗的细胞和分子景观。RSF模型为风险分层提供了稳健工具，同时将RAD51确定为恢复放射敏感性和逆转免疫抑制的潜在治疗靶点，特别是在高风险、免疫冷肿瘤中。
